Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (HorizonLedger), Tom Reeves (HorizonLedger), Sara Lin (HorizonLedger)

summary: Introductory SDK integration walkthrough focused on quickstart auth patterns (API key, Vault, GCP Workload Identity), Console usage for environment and model pinning, and Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching, prefix/KV caching). Customer aims to run a small pilot (pilot scope: internal search assist across transaction metadata) with emphasis on data residency and KMS-managed encryption.
topics:
1) Auth options and CI secret handling
2) SDK quickstart Python and TypeScript
3) Console environment setup and sandbox
4) Optimize knobs: batching, cache, quantization recommendations
5) Security/compliance questions: SOC2/KMS/SSO
6) Next steps and action items
transcript:
00:00 Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're gonna run through a short sprint-zero style integration, auth patterns, quickstart SDK samples in python and typescript, and a quick drift of the console. (laughs)
00:18 Aisha Khan: cool sounds good. we have Tom and Sara here too, Tom will be doing the platform lift, Sara will ask security stuff.
00:28 Carlos Ruiz: hi all, carlos from redwood, i'm the se today. quick question before we dive, are you planning hosted API or private deployment for pilot?
00:40 Aisha Khan: for pilot we'll start hosted, but we need to validate data residency and KMS workflows; long term likely private or dedicated if perf looks good.
00:55 Carlos Ruiz: got it. hosted + KMS integration is a common path, you can use redwood's customer-managed KMS via our console or pass-through with an HSM in private deploys — note, some overlap in naming in transcript here "K V cash" sorry that's my accent.
01:15 Tom Reeves: right, and we have GCP infra, so workload identity is preferred over long-lived service account keys.
01:25 Maya Patel: perfect, we have a quickstart for GCP Workload Identity in our docs, and the SDK supports it indirectly via ADC. we'll link that. ok jumping into code — first python quickstart.
01:40 Carlos Ruiz: sample snippet — set REDWOOD_API_KEY in env for small tests, but for CI we recommend short-lived tokens from vault or workload identity binding. here's a python example...
01:55 Speaker 1: "code shown" (python)
02:10 Carlos Ruiz: note the client.init(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) pattern, and then we show a streaming call for generation. for batching we include a examples/batcher.py that uses the sdk's bulk_generate helper.
02:40 Aisha Khan: when you say bulk_generate, is that client-side or server-side batching?
02:50 Carlos Ruiz: it's client helper that creates multi-request payloads to the API; on the server side our runtime does continuous batching and will also pack short-seq requests. optimize will recommend batch sizes based on latency/cost tradeoffs.
03:10 Sara Lin: what's the default retention for logs and user prompts in hosted?
03:18 Maya Patel: hosted defaults are 30 days for request logs, you can request longer retention via enterprise plan; sensitive fields can be redacted client-side and we support tokenization patterns. we'll include the retention doc link.
03:40 Tom Reeves: for env setup, how do we isolate between staging and prod in the console?
03:48 Maya Patel: console supports multiple environments in the org — sandbox, staging, prod — and you can pin model versions per route and set rollout policies. we usually create a sandbox project for pilots, which we'll provision for you.
04:05 Carlos Ruiz: switching to TypeScript — same auth patterns, env var or short-lived token. snippet: import {Redwood} from '@redwoodinc/sdk'
04:18 Carlos Ruiz: typescript example uses node's process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY and also shows a fetch wrapper for streaming tokens.
04:30 Aisha Khan: any sample CI snippet for rotating creds?
04:36 Carlos Ruiz: yes, we have terraform+github actions example that exchanges a service account token for a short-lived redwood key using our token exchange endpoint, we can share that repo link.
04:55 Sara Lin: about KMS — do you allow customer provided keys for model payload encryption at rest?
05:03 Maya Patel: yes, for private deployments you can bring-your-own-KMS and for hosted we offer customer-managed keys for certain enterprise tiers; we'll follow up with the exact SLA and the KMS whitepaper.
05:20 Carlos Ruiz: also worth noting, if you want to keep prompt data out of logs we support prefix/KV caching so you can store user vectors locally and only send non-sensitive parts. small mis-transcripts may say KV "cash" earlier.
05:40 Aisha Khan: can you explain KV caching a bit more — where does the cache live?
05:48 Carlos Ruiz: cache can be server-side in dedicated pools or client-side. the common pattern: client stores persistent KV for user prefixes, sends cache handle rather than raw prompt, runtime rehydrates KV to reduce token count. big win for cost.
06:10 Tom Reeves: interesting. and quantization guidance — for our workload (short sequences, high QPS), what do you suggest?
06:20 Carlos Ruiz: for short sequences and high RPS, 4-bit quant models with optimized kernels are usually a sweet spot, they reduce memory and increase throughput; Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per model workload.
06:40 Aisha Khan: okay, what about observability — how do we trace per-request latency back to routes/models?
06:48 Maya Patel: console has per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and distributed traces you can hook into with our tracing headers. we can show a live demo of the console dashboard in a follow-up or right now if you want.
07:05 Sara Lin: we need audit logs down to the token-level and SSO integration with our Okta tenant.
07:13 Maya Patel: SSO/SAML is supported and we can map roles to RBAC in the console. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM, and we can set retention policies.
07:30 Carlos Ruiz: quick demo — i'll switch over to the Console, (screen share) sandbox project > keys > create ephemeral key. steps: create env, pin model gptx-3-redwood (typo sometimes), set route to use model, link to rollout policy.
07:55 Aisha Khan: can you show how to add KMS there?
08:02 Maya Patel: under settings > security > key management, you can link a cloud KMS; for GCP it's an IAM role with allowCryptoKeyEncrypto, etc. small note: the console UI may refer to 'key ring' differently.
08:20 Tom Reeves: latency question — what are typical p95 latencies for 1k token outputs on a dedicated pool?
08:30 Carlos Ruiz: common p95 numbers: 100-200ms per 1 token at scale for streaming, but that is model-specific. for p95 of 1k tokens we'd look at end-to-end numbers; we'll run a benchmark for you.
08:50 Aisha Khan: what's the process to migrate to Dedicated later?
08:55 Maya Patel: migration is straightforward, we can map routes to dedicated pools and set autoscaling policies; can be scheduled with rolling canary to minimize disruption.
09:10 Carlos Ruiz: ok pivot: let's show quickstart repo structure — /python/examples/quickstart.py, /ts/examples/quickstart.ts, docs/ci/rotate-keys.md
09:25 Carlos Ruiz: i'll paste a small python snippet for streaming and a TS snippet for batch embeddings.
09:35 Speaker 2: "code shown" (typescript)
09:55 Aisha Khan: you mentioned Optimize — will it auto-tune batch sizes or do we have to change code?
10:01 Carlos Ruiz: Optimize provides recommendations and you can opt-in to automated policies. there's an SDK flag for adaptive batching but many customers prefer manual pinning initially.
10:20 Sara Lin: when you say automated policies, can they be rolled back if quality regresses?
10:26 Maya Patel: yes, rollouts canary and automatic fallback policies exist — if a new quant model shows regression on eval prompt sets we'll fallback to the pinned version.
10:40 Tom Reeves: is there support for per-tenant prompt redaction before data hits your servers?
10:46 Carlos Ruiz: yes, we recommend either client-side redaction libraries or a preprocessor microservice that strips PHI. we have an example preprocessor you can deploy in your VPC.
11:05 Aisha Khan: what's the recommended approach for our CI environment secrets? we use github actions and terraform.
11:13 Carlos Ruiz: best practice: store short-lived tokens in GitHub secrets via actions secrets, rotate using a workflow that hits your vault and exchanges for ephemeral redwood token. we have a sample GH action.
11:30 Sara Lin: any required security questionnaires like VA/PT or SOC2 questionnaires?
11:36 Maya Patel: we supply an ATO pack for enterprise and SOC2/ISO attestation documents. we'll send the standard security questionnaire and an extension pack for KMS & private deployments.
11:55 Carlos Ruiz: ok, let's run a short live test — Maya, can you provision the sandbox key while i paste the TS snippet?
12:05 Maya Patel: provisioning now, you'll get an ephemeral key link in the chat. note: ephemeral keys last 24 hours by default.
12:22 Aisha Khan: got it, key received. we'll try the python script first.
12:30 Tom Reeves: heads up, our network blocks non-443 outbound sometimes, is there a web proxy configuration?
12:38 Carlos Ruiz: the SDK supports proxy env variables (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY). if you need mTLS we can discuss private deployment.
12:55 Aisha Khan: running the script now... hmm one sec — i see a TLS error in our CI runner.
13:03 Maya Patel: try updating root CAs, but also check corporate egress interception; if needed we can whitelist our IP ranges or provide VPC connectors for private deployment.
13:25 Tom Reeves: this is helpful. ok two more questions: throttling and rate limits, and how quota billing works.
13:32 Maya Patel: hosted has rate limits per account and per key, quota consumption is per-token generation and per-embedding unit. Console shows projected costs and token-level billing.
13:48 Sara Lin: does Redwood support on-prem for air-gapped? we have one regulated pod that may require on-prem.
13:55 Maya Patel: yes, on-prem packages are available and include a private control plane options with offline KMS/HSM integration.
14:10 Carlos Ruiz: last section: troubleshooting tips — common causes for hangs are KV cache lookups blocked or long-running preprocessor RPCs, also watch out for sequence length misconfiguration in client.
14:28 Aisha Khan: great, i'm going to sync with our infra folks, but overall this looks doable. thanks.
14:36 Maya Patel: recap — we'll send sandbox creds, security docs (SOC2/KMS), python/TS sample repo, and schedule a perf benchmark early April. next call to be scheduled after your infra validation.
14:52 Tom Reeves: i'll loop in our infra and set up the benchmark scope doc.
14:58 Sara Lin: thanks everyone, appreciate the KMS details.
15:03 Carlos Ruiz: thanks all, i'll drop the repo and GH actions snippet in chat.
15:10 Maya Patel: action items in chat as well, we'll follow up with calendar invite for benchmark. bye!
15:15 Meeting ended.
